title: Hundred Grid Shader
description: Cut a tenth into hundredths and a hundredth into thousandths, shade any squares of the right count, and read a grid by columns and squares.
modes: none. One flow, one phase at a time. The host mounts a phase (phase prop). With navigableDots true, or no phase, the child may jump phases with the dots (user mode); otherwise the dots show progress and the teacher agent drives window.toolApi (AI mode). The last phase, and a whole lesson, end on the summary page, where Free play and Play again sit. With navDots the dots are controls in AI mode too: a tap on a dot starts that phase.

stage.sizing: the frame is min(100vw, 177.78vh) wide and min(100vh, 56.25vw) tall (dvh where supported); the svg fills it. Nothing scrolls.

bands.header: 0 to 80. One line: the tool name, a measured dot, the phase concept; Hint, sound and restart as round controls far right.
bands.canvas: 92 to 640. One rounded card holding the key at its top right (Answer, Close, Enter, Next, or the Yes / No keys; no question bar), the working area (the whole card until Answer is tapped) and the answer drawer that slides in from the right; the summary page covers it at the end.
bands.footer: 652 to 900. The mascot at the far left on its ground line, the speech bubble beside it (y 656 to 892, the question and every line, printed), one small dot per phase at the right.

zones.layout: board, key only: no question bar, only its key at the right end of the top row (the question is on the bubble); the working area is the whole card (64, 108, 1472 x 520) until the child taps Answer, when the answer drawer (as tall as the working area, the key on its top row reading Close) slides in from the right
zones.controls: circles r 28 at cx 1388, 1460, 1532, cy 40: Hint (data-control again), sound, restart; 72-unit finger boxes
zones.dots: one small dot per phase at the footer's right (72-unit finger boxes, centred on the bubble), no text; in user AND AI mode each is a button (data-control phase-dot, data-phase k) that starts its phase

stage.noSidebar: There is no sidebar. The canvas takes every unit the chrome can spare.
stage.noScoreBox: There is no score box on the stage. The score leaves on finished and onComplete and is shown once, as stars on the summary page.

writeup.why: Read and shade hundredths on a hundred grid, writing them as fractions and as decimals, and see thousandths come from cutting a hundredth into ten.
writeup.look: A full ten by ten grid at the left, the Columns and squares counter under it, a fraction card and a decimal card at its right, and a zoomed square on the last phase.
writeup.stage: Three bands across 1600 by 900. The header runs 0 to 80 and is one line only: 'Hundred Grid Shader' in ink at the far left, a small dot set clear of the name, the phase title beside the dot on the same line, the host's navigation, and sound and restart as three round controls at the far right. The canvas runs 92 to 746, one rounded card on the paper colour. At its top left, at x sixty-four, y 108 and 330 by 76, sits the running count: how many squares are shaded, rising as the child drags and falling as it clears. On the last phase it counts thin slices instead. It is never a score. The working area is 1086 by 528 at x sixty-four, y 202. The grid is 480 by 480 at x 110, y 226, ten columns of ten squares, every square 48 across, ruled in near-black and labelled Whole above its top edge. Shaded squares are deep blue; unshaded squares stay warm white. The lifted column stands at x 640, y 226, its ten squares spread with small gaps, labelled 1 tenth above and 1 hundredth on its top square. The Columns and squares counter sits under the grid at y 716 in ink. The fraction card and the decimal card stand at x 900, y 300, one above the other, turning green when the child's answer matches the shading. On the last phase the zoomed square is drawn as a strip 400 long and 60 tall at x 640, y 520, cut into ten thin slices by near-black lines, each labelled 1 thousandth, with a fine line back to the square it came from. The Cut column, Scatter and Zoom buttons sit in a row at x 640, y 440. Down the right of the canvas, in the same rectangle on every phase and never animated in or out, the question sits above the answer slot at x 1186, y 250 (356 by 92) that holds what the child has given, and under it the pad at x 1170, y 368 (388 by 363). The pad is twelve number keys three across with a point key and a fraction bar key, for setting a number of hundredths or thousandths, or for typing a fraction or a decimal into the answer slot. The footer runs 758 to 900: the voice caption at the far left with its speaking dot beside it, measuring its own wrap and dropping a type size rather than spilling, and the phase bar at the right with the question count under it. There is no sidebar and no score box anywhere, and nothing is ever written over the working area. Content colours are the chapter's own, and the tools of this chapter share them. A decimal or fraction the question gives is deep blue, with the shaded parts that show it. The result the working reaches, a decimal, a fraction, a sum, a difference or what is left, is green, with its shaded parts. Ten of one place traded for one of the next, a carry in adding or a trade in taking away, is vermilion. A zero written after the point to line decimals up is violet, and so is the point written after a whole number before those zeros. The part taken away, used or poured out is rose. The digit, place or step being worked on now, and the first place where two decimals differ, are amber. A zero holding a place open inside a number is grey, and nothing else on the stage is ever grey. An unshaded part stays warm white inside its near-black outline, the decimal point is near-black ink, and anything dimmed fades to half strength rather than turning grey. Chrome never borrows one of them, and each of those readings survives with the colour taken away, because a part is told by its written label, Given, Answer, Carry, Trade, Added zero, Taken away, Left or Place holder, before it is told by its colour.
writeup.finish: The card shows the last grid beside its fraction over 100 and its decimal, with one square lifted and sliced into thousandths.

phases.win: the card shows 1/100 and 0.01, and the column reads ten hundredths make one tenth
phases.does: taps Cut column, counts the squares in the lifted column, and shades one square
phases.goal: a tenth cut into ten equal parts gives hundredths, and 10 hundredths make 1 tenth
phases.says: One column is one tenth. Cut it into ten. What is one square?
phases.check: Away from the screen: which is smaller, one tenth of a chocolate bar or one hundredth of it? How do you know?
phases.feels: a column falling apart into ten little squares
phases.hands: Cut a paper square into ten equal strips, then cut one strip into ten small squares. Lay the small squares beside the whole square and count how many would cover it.
phases.tries: First rung: count the squares in one column. Second rung: count the columns in the grid. Third rung: the same task on a column already lifted out, before the whole grid returns.

writeup.delight: On the third phase, when the child taps Scatter, the shaded squares lift off the grid, drift about like leaves and settle in new places, and the decimal card stays exactly as it was.
writeup.opening: Every mount comes up already furnished for its phase with the grid in place. On the first phase the grid is empty with one column outlined in amber and the words one tenth above it. On the second a shading is already on the grid and the Columns and squares counter is hidden. On the third the grid is empty and the question card names a number of hundredths. On the fourth one square is outlined in amber and the Zoom button is lit. One thing moves, once: the outlined column or square, or the grid's first square, gives one slow pulse while the voice speaks its opening line, and a finger on it is the whole way in.
writeup.freePlay: Any shading of the grid, scattered or in columns, and any square zoomed and sliced. Nothing to get right, no target and no timer. The child is left with the same stage and every control unlocked.
writeup.practice: Eight items over the four phases, easy first, on hundredths of a tenth, reading and shading grids, and thousandths.

onWrong.marks: Nothing is marked, nothing resets, no colour means good or bad. The child's answer stays; the pad re-opens after the traceback.
tracebacks: Phase 1: The cut column's squares are numbered one by one under 1 tenth, ending on 10 hundredths; a tenth shaded in hundredths fills one column, numbered; one square is ringed beside its column and the cards end on 1/100 and 0.01.
Phase 2: Each full column is lit and labelled 10 as the counter adds in tens, the single squares join one by one, and the cards end on the hundredths as a fraction and a decimal.

Phase 3: The counter reads the child's shading in hundredths, a second grid shades the asked number of single squares beside it, and the cards end on the asked hundredths; for the two children each grid is counted to 14.
Phase 4: The zoomed square's slices are numbered, the decimal card lights its third place after the point in amber with grey zeros holding the places, and the cards end on the thousandths.

voice.opening: A hundred small squares, all the same size.
voice.onFreePlay: Free play. Shade, scatter and zoom as you like.
voice.onMiss: the item's own miss line, then the phase's two ladder rungs, shown at once UNDER the pinned instruction and kept until the child acts again
voice.onFinish: Tenths into hundredths, and hundredths into thousandths.
voice.rules: Silent: nothing is spoken (no device speech, no recorded clips, no Tap to start cover). The speech bubble is the guide: every instruction and hint is one printed page, numbers as words. The lesson is action-driven in every mode: a guide step's instruction stays until the child does the act it names; a wrong act shows that step's hint under the pinned instruction, a wrong answer the next rung of its ladder, and the hint stays unchanged until the child acts again; a right answer's next question, a phase's next phase and the summary's rows follow by themselves after a short celebration. The header's Hint key shows the step's hint or the next rung on demand. What is heard is sound effects (Web Audio), switched by the sound button, on in every mode. In classroom mode nothing waits for a tap except the pieces of a long line (the blinking arrow; a tap, Enter, Space, ArrowRight or PageDown on the bubble shows the next piece), and a tap on the bubble when nothing waits is the teacher's skip.

guide.playsOn: guide steps on phase 1, 2, 3, 4: the phase opens on its first instruction and waits for the child's act (getState guideStep, guideSteps, guideOn); the agent's check() performs the current step; the last act opens the first question. Other phases open on their printed teach lines, and a demo phase waits for the child's own act.

palette.rule: A content colour fills countable things only and chrome never borrows one; coloured numerals and words take a deeper ink of their colour (4.5:1).

items.planQuestion: One column of a hundred grid is one tenth of the grid. How many hundredths is one column?

question.en: Each square is one hundredth, so how many hundredths make the cut column?

items.planQuestion: How many hundredths make one tenth?

question.en: Shade as many hundredths as make one tenth, then press Enter.
3 squares of the grid are shaded, so what decimal is that?

items.planQuestion: A hundred grid has 5 full columns and 3 more squares shaded. Write the shaded part as a fraction and as a decimal.

question.en: What decimal does the shaded part of this grid show?

items.planQuestion: A hundred grid has 6 full columns shaded and nothing else. Write the shaded part as a decimal.

question.en: Now write this new shading as a decimal.

items.planAnswer: 60 of the 100 squares, 60/100, which is 0.60 or 0.6

items.planQuestion: A hundred grid has 2 full columns and 9 more squares shaded. Write the shaded part as a fraction and as a decimal.

question.en: Which fraction of the whole grid is shaded?

items.planQuestion: Shade a hundred grid to show 0.04.

question.en: Shade squares on the grid to show 0.04, then press Enter.

items.planQuestion: How many squares of a hundred grid do you shade to show 0.21?

question.en: Now show 0.21 on the grid the same way.

items.planQuestion: Two children show 0.14 on hundred grids. One shades a full column and 4 more squares. The other shades 14 squares scattered about. Who is right?

question.en: Asha shades a column and 4 squares, Bina 14 scattered squares: who shows 0.14?

items.planAnswer: Both are right. Each shaded 14 of the 100 squares, and which squares does not matter

items.planQuestion: How many thousandths make one hundredth?

question.en: How many thousandths make one hundredth?

items.planQuestion: One hundredth is cut into 10 equal parts and 3 of them are shaded. Write the shaded part as a fraction and as a decimal.

question.en: 3 of the 10 slices of this hundredth are shaded: what decimal is that?

items.planQuestion: Write 41 thousandths as a fraction and as a decimal.

scoring.wrong: costs nothing, never marked, counted only for first try accuracy
scoring.stars: one for finishing, two at sixty per cent right first time, three at ninety; hidden with the first-try line by showScore false
scoring.phaseMount: a mount scores every phase it plays, from its phase to the last (+5 a question; phases of 3, 3, 3, 3 questions)
scoring.finishCard: stars and the Right first time line under the phase rows on the summary page

hostContract.phase: absent (not a finite number): the whole lesson, phases one to 4 in a row, the summary page at the end, finished once. Present: rounded and clamped to one to 4; the tool starts at that phase and, as the NCERT tools do, walks on by itself after each phase's last question (its closing line, then 1.4 s), in user and AI mode alike, through phase 4 to the summary page (a tool with nextKey, runtime r48+: in user mode it waits for the child's blinking Next key instead, after every question and every phase, and the last phase's key opens the summary; AI mode, and a host that mounts one phase without navigableDots, walk on by themselves); finished once, from the summary page.
hostContract.navigableDots: true (or no phase): user mode, the phase dots are controls; otherwise AI mode, the dots show progress and the agent drives window.toolApi.

onProgress.done: questions right so far in this phase

hostContract.emits: every event is dispatched on window and, when framed, posted to window.parent as { type: 'event', name, detail }
